analysis.title: GS Singer - Weekly Best of GS Earnings Season, Single Stock Inbounds, Brazil, Energy, Midterms & Capital Markets 9 Oct 2026
key_insights: No single theme dominated the week. Macro attention centered on the move in Brazil, with a rate reprieve (10-year yield flattish on the week) and mixed headlines on AI funding and revenue.
Earnings season is starting slowly. 7% of the S&P 500 by market cap reports next week (heavy financials skew), followed by 14% the week after.
Consensus expects Q3 S&P 500 y/y EPS growth of 27%, versus 33% in Q2. AI infrastructure spending accounts for 50% of the growth this quarter. AI monetization and productivity remain the key theme.
Earnings distortions from private equity stakes should fade in Q3. Tariff refunds continue to give a modest boost to earnings.

Single-stock inbound interest this week: mobile carriers (T, VZ, TMUS) after the SPCX spectrum deal, PLTR after an upgrade to Buy, PEP after a guidance downgrade, CMG/SBUX on a potential restaurant tie-up, BSP (+25% on Wednesday), HUM (improved Medicare star ratings) and DAL (tightening fuel costs).
Brazil drew the most macro interest. EWZ printed over $8bn of volume on Monday, more than IWM and TLT, and by Thursday had its largest flow on record. The ETF desk sees a strong bid.

The baskets team is pushing Brazil Rate Sensitive Stocks (GSBZRATE) and Brazil Domestics (GSCBBZEN) after the first round of Brazil elections. Some exotic trades (EWZ higher, EUR lower) are also getting attention.
The energy complex continues to move higher on geopolitics. GS's energy team likes 10 stocks into year end: OXY, CCP, PR (E&P), PWR, DUK, BKR, GLNG (power), DINO (refining), TRP and AR (midstream).

Senate midterms: prediction markets imply a 65% chance Democrats win a Senate majority, which requires a net gain of 4 seats. Polls show Democrats ahead in 7 Republican-held seats and all of their own close races, but most are within the margin of error.

House midterms: prediction markets imply more than a 90% chance Democrats net the three seats needed for a majority. Democrats lead the generic ballot by an average of 8.9pp, about a 12pp swing from the 2.6pp House Republican popular vote margin in 2024.

The IBD team sees the midterms as a potential clearing event. Markets have historically underperformed into midterms (median -3.5% in the month before, since 1974) and outperformed after (median +6.5% in the 4 months following), which sets up well for ECM into year end.

Charts flagged: the recent rally has hurt given where net exposure sits, Brazil volumes exploded, a clear gap between the market and the market ex-AI, and French CDS and NVDA CDS trading at essentially the same levels.
